# A ten-point diamond filter: Helly 8 to 9 and an exact coarse/fine depth gap

This strengthens the already audited eleven-point example without changing it. There is a lattice-convex ten-point P' subset Z^3 with h(P')=8 and a rational Jensen-affine height g whose integral graph has nine points and Helly number 9. Its simplex product has no zero-mass fine fibers. For every s>=1 its exact maximal fine and coarse depths are respectively Gamma_s/9 and Gamma_s/2.

The fine integer rank is four; the coarse integer rank is three. The coarse problem admits a fractional-height center that the fine problem excludes. This is an obstruction to deleting an integer condition while retaining the original measure/depth guarantee, not an OC counterexample.

## 1. Restrict the eleven-point support

Use the points p_i and heights g_i in `candidate 5c9190df7c42c598`. Put

    W={p_0,p_1,p_3,p_4,p_5,p_6,p_7,p_8,p_10},
    Q'=conv(W),
    P'=Q' intersect Z^3.

The earlier exact inequalities contain Q'. Their complete integer set is the eleven-point P. The omitted point p_9 is outside Q' because y+z=3 there while y+z<=2 on W. The other omitted point satisfies

    p_2=(p_0+p_6)/2=(p_1+p_3)/2.

Therefore

    P'=W union {p_2},    |P'|=10.                         (1)

Every W point is exposed in Q' by the previously printed integer normal table. Thus p_2 is its only nonvertex integer point. Its minimal face is the diamond

    F=Q' intersect {y=0}=conv{p_0,p_1,p_3,p_6},

and p_2 lies in relint(F). In (x,z) coordinates these four vertices are (0,1),(1,0),(1,2),(2,1), with center (1,1).

Restrict the old g to P'. It is Jensen-affine, either by restriction or directly: on F it equals (3-x-z)/2, and every other P' point is a vertex. Its only fractional value is g_2=1/2. Hence

    T'={(p,g(p)):p in P', g(p) in Z}=W_hat.              (2)

The graph hull conv(T') has exactly its nine vertices as integer points in R^4, as the old exact verifier also checks directly. It is full-dimensional. Since T' itself is in convex position, h(T')=9: the nine deletion hulls are an exact critical family.

## 2. The original Helly number and component loss are exact

The five-point diamond D={p_0,p_1,p_2,p_3,p_6} has h(D)=3. Three noncollinear corners give the lower bound. For the upper bound, its four corners have the center in their deletion kernel; any four-point subset containing the center fails convex position because three diamond corners contain an opposite pair and hence contain the center in their convex hull. A critical witness must be in convex position, and its subsets remain critical, so no witness of size four or larger exists.

For finite source sets the union inequality

    h(S_1 union ... union S_m) <= sum_i h(S_i)           (3)

follows by selecting, from a source-infeasible convex family, a subfamily excluding each S_i and then taking their union. Decomposing P' into D and the five remaining singleton vertices gives

    h(P')<=3+5=8.

For equality take V=W minus {p_3}, an eight-point subset. Each V point is exposed, so it does not lie in its own deletion hull. The omitted corner p_3 is outside conv(V): on the supporting face y=0 the remaining three corners have z<=1, whereas p_3 has z=2. The center p_2 is outside conv(V minus {p_0}): that face now has only p_1,p_6, whose segment does not contain p_2. Thus the deletion kernel of V contains no point of P', proving

    h(P')=8,       h(T')=9.                              (4)

In dependence-component terms, the diamond with its center is the sole nonsingleton component, of affine rank two, and the other five vertices are isolated. The filter changes the diamond's Helly contribution from three to four; it leaves the five singleton contributions intact. This is a concrete failure of a total budget based on the unfiltered Helly number. It does not refute a connected-support-only variant.

## 3. A full-dimensional product with all fine fibers positive

Let K be any full-dimensional s-simplex, s>=1, with volume V_K and centroid c_K. Define

    C_s=conv(W_hat) times K subset R^3_p x R_u x R^s_x.  (5)

This is a full-dimensional convex body of dimension 4+s. At every coarse integer p in P', Jensen affinity forces its u-fiber to the single value g(p). Conversely every such graph point belongs to conv(W_hat), and the product in (5) supplies the full K there. Thus

    (C_s)_p={g(p)} times K,        p in P'.               (6)

Every full (s+1)-dimensional coarse fiber volume is zero, although the entire ambient body is full-dimensional.

For the fine source impose (p,u) in Z^3 times Z. Equations (1)--(2) give EXACTLY nine fine fibers, all equal to K, with total intrinsic H_s mass 9V_K. Every generating fiber belongs to the fine mixed set, so C_s is exactly the convex hull of that set. There is no zero-mass point fiber in this strengthened construction.

The finite isolation and simplex-cap proof in `candidate 3b375252ca398671` applies with its outlier cap omitted. Specifically, the exposing normals have unit integer gaps, and

    lambda_r(x)-1/(s+1)+2 n_i dot(p-p_i)>=0

isolates each of the s+1 canonical simplex caps at its W base from every other positive fine fiber. Those caps cover all nine fibers and each has mass Gamma_s V_K. The own-simplex centroid lower bound matches this cover, giving

    max fine depth = Gamma_s/9.                          (7)

This conclusion has only the ordinary continuous simplex-depth dependency. It does not use the paired-tail theorem in the next section.

## 4. Exact coarse maximum at the newly eligible center

Now drop only the condition u in Z and use the actual coarse source C_s intersect (Z^3 times R^(s+1)), with its intrinsic H_s measure. It has TEN equal K fibers, by (6), and total mass 10V_K. In particular it includes

    a_2=(p_2,1/2,c_K),

which is not a fine mixed point.

We use the proved auxiliary theorem `candidate 732b11a769399016`, Section 1: for a uniform convex body K and any nonzero x-normal v, its centroid tail F satisfies

    F(t)+F(-t)>=2 Gamma_s    for every real t.            (8)

That theorem's external ordinary localization dependency and complete scalar proof remain as recorded there. No assertion of (8) is needed for the standalone fine-depth calculation (7).

The five coarse graph bases in the facet y=0 consist of a_2's base and TWO symmetric pairs about it:

    (p_0,g_0)+(p_6,g_6)=2(p_2,1/2),
    (p_1,g_1)+(p_3,g_3)=2(p_2,1/2).                     (9)

Consider any closed cap containing a_2 and shift its boundary to a_2 if necessary, which only decreases its mass. If its x-normal is nonzero, its restrictions to each pair in (9) have opposite centroid thresholds. Each pair therefore contributes at least 2 Gamma_s V_K by (8), and the own K fiber contributes at least Gamma_s V_K. The remaining five coarse fibers contribute nonnegative mass. If the x-normal is zero, the closed cap includes the whole own fiber and at least one whole K from each pair, hence mass at least 3V_K >=5 Gamma_s V_K. Consequently

    depth_coarse(a_2)>=Gamma_s/2.                        (10)

For the matching upper bound at EVERY point of the p_2 fiber, use the s+1 caps

    lambda_r(x)-1/(s+1)-2y>=0.                          (11)

They isolate the facet y=0 from every other coarse fiber and capture the same canonical simplex cap in each of its five K fibers. Each has mass exactly 5 Gamma_s V_K, and they cover the entire p_2 fiber.

At any other coarse base p_i in W, its exposing normal remains strict against p_2. Indeed at least one of the two disjoint midpoint pairs in (9) omits p_i, so p_2 belongs to conv(W minus {p_i}); the old exposure gap is therefore still at least one. The caps from Section 3 isolate its simplex caps from ALL other coarse fibers, now including p_2. They give depth at most Gamma_s/10 at every such point.

Together these statements prove the global equality

    max coarse depth = depth_coarse(a_2) = Gamma_s/2.     (12)

All normal directions and closed-boundary cases are included. The exact ratio of the two global maxima is

    (max fine depth)/(max coarse depth)=2/9.              (13)

Dropping integrality has added only one of the ten coarse mass fibers, but it has admitted a new center and increased maximal depth by a factor 9/2.

## 5. Consequence and verification

For s>=2, the already proved Gamma comparison gives

    Gamma_s/9 < Gamma_(s+1)/8,

with equality when s=1. Thus (7) obstructs a naive transfer of the rank-three, continuous-dimension-(s+1) target to the ORIGINAL fine source. The actual coarse source has the much larger depth (12), so no coarse OC assertion is contradicted. The actual fine OC target is Gamma_s/16, below (7).

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_ten_point_diamond_filter_depth_gap.py` checks the exact support reduction, diamond kernel and original critical eight-subset, integrality, all exposure gaps including the added coarse center, both lifted midpoint pairs, and the source masses/cap constants. The two prior exact verifiers supply the full lattice-hull and ambient-rank checks. The all-cap lower bound (10) explicitly uses the independently proved paired-tail theorem.
